t: Founded when Hugh Capet was elected king in 987, it was ruled by Capetians, Valois and Bourbons for more than 800 years.
Its kings grew a small domain around Paris into Europe's most populous kingdom through war, marriage, inheritance and law.
Louis XIV's Versailles made France the model of European monarchy, but unreformed debt led to the Revolution of 1789.
dyk: The Estates-General, the kingdom's assembly of clergy, nobles and commons, did not meet at all between 1614 and 1789, when its summons opened the Revolution.
ev: Hugh Capet is elected and crowned king, founding the Capetian dynasty
Philip II Augustus defeats Otto IV and his allies at the Battle of Bouvines
The Hundred Years' War with England begins
Joan of Arc relieves Orléans and Charles VII is crowned at Reims
Henry IV's Edict of Nantes grants toleration to the Huguenots
Louis XIV moves the court and government to Versailles
The Estates-General meets and the Revolution begins
The monarchy is abolished and the First Republic proclaimed

f.capital: Paris; Versailles (seat of court and government, 1682–1789)
